item.title: Lady of Elche: A 2,400-year-old bust of a mysterious 'highborn' woman from pre-Roman Spain
item.description: The mysterious Lady of Elche was crafted from a large limestone block before the Romans ruled Spain.

item.title: 3 rivers merge into striking half-and-half waterway in Guyana — Earth from space
item.description: A 2023 satellite photo highlights the point where a trio of rivers converges in Guyana. One of the waterways has been significantly altered by mining waste, creating a striking color contrast.

item.title: Vanuatu's 'barefoot volcanologist' stands at ash- and sulfur-spewing Mount Yasur in award-winning photograph
item.description: Elle Leontiev's image of Philip, a self-taught volcanologist who has lived on Mount Yasur his whole life, has won the Portraiture category of the Open competition of the Sony World Photography Awards 2026.

item.title: Every ant is a queen in this parasitic species — and they reproduce by cloning themselves and hijacking other ant colonies
item.description: A rare Japanese ant is the only species known to lack female workers and males; all of its young develop into parasitic queens that try to take over other colonies.

item.title: 'Blood moon' total lunar eclipse dazzles millions around the world (photos)
item.description: Here are the first images of the March 3 'blood moon' total lunar eclipse visible over North America, Australia, and eastern Asia.

item.title: Gold coin discovered by a metal detectorist in the UK may have been dropped by a Viking invader from the Great Heathen Army
item.description: A gold coin featuring the son of Charlemagne may have been a keepsake from a Viking invader who fought in the Great Heathen Army.

item.title: 'Collective hum' of black holes could mend our broken understanding of the universe, physicists say
item.description: Ripples in the fabric of space-time called gravitational waves may be the key to solving the Hubble tension — one of the biggest nagging problems in physics.

item.title: Stone Age woman was buried like a man, revealing flexible gender roles 7,000 years ago in Hungary
item.description: A study of 125 skeletons from two Neolithic cemeteries in Hungary has revealed that men and women had clear gender roles — but sometimes those roles were fluid.

item.title: Mysterious 'little red dots' discovered by James Webb telescope may be the first stars in the universe on the verge of collapse
item.description: A new study suggests that "little red dots" spied by the James Webb Space Telescope could be the universe's short-lived first generation of gigantic stars, challenging an existing theory.

item.title: Prehistoric water-dwelling weirdo with sideways teeth and a twisted jaw was already a 'living fossil' 275 million years ago
item.description: Scientists have described Tanyka amnicola, a newly identified species of prehistoric creature that lived 275 million years ago and had a bizarre twisted jaw with sideways-facing teeth.
